The '''Republic Starfighter Corps''' was the [[Starfighter combat/Legends|starfighter]] [[Starfighter Corps/Legends|corps]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] that was organized under the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], although it was considered a separate fighting force. The [[Corps/Legends|Corps]] served as an independent branch until after the [[New Sith Wars]], when the Republic Starfighter Corps was transferred to the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] in accordance with the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]]. The Republic Starfighter Corps was restored as an independent branch in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] with the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. However, after the [[Declaration of a New Order|establishment]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] became subordinated to the requirements of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].

==History==
===The Sith Wars===
Part of the Republic Military, throughout its history the Republic Starfighter Corps fulfilled both planetary-based orbital defense and fleet-based deep-space combat. Traditionally it was far more involved in the former role than the latter, it being far more difficult to attach starfighters to fleets than it was to operate them from the surface of a planet. Consequently, the Republic Navy tended to disdain dedicated [[Carrier/Legends|carriers]] while the Republic Starfighter Corps operated long-range, [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable, heavily-armed [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]] from planetary bases.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

For much of galactic history, however, snubfighters were absent from deep-space engagements: many of the advantages of snubfighters disappeared in the great distances between opposing squadrons of [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]]. Starfighters that were designed for fleet engagements were traditionally short-ranged superiority fighters like the [[S-100 Stinger-class starfighter|S-100 ''Stinger''-class starfighter]], intended for scouting ahead of assault fleets and countering attacking snubfighters with superior speed and mobility. During the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], ''Stinger''-class starfighters duelled with the [[Blade-class starfighter|''Blade''-class starfighters]] of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

From the [[Mandalorian Wars]] for nearly four thousand years, the [[Aurek-class tactical strikefighter|''Aurek''-class tactical strikefighter]] was the Republic's standard planet-based "hyperspace snub", with the [[S-250 Chela-class starfighter|S-250 ''Chela''-class starfighter]] fulfilling a similar role. For many centuries, however, commanders were sceptical of the ability of snubfighters to decisively impact on a space battle. When anti-ship missile capability was needed, naval commanders preferred specialist [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] starfighters, large, complex and heavy craft built around powerful sensor arrays and days-long mission profiles, designed to track down enemy fleets and launch surprise attacks. Naval wisdom held for centuries that this was the only scenario in which [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedo]] runs could penetrate defensive fighter screens and [[Flak/Legends|flak]] defenses.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

In the aftermath of the [[Ruusan campaign]], the final actions of the [[New Sith Wars]], the Republic Starfighter Corps was transferred into the [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] while the rest of the Republic Military were dissolved.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===Clone Wars===
The Republic Starfighter Corps was restored as a independent branch in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] with the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Tactically speaking, the Corps was fully integrated into the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] and the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]].<ref name="The Clone Wars Campaign Guide">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Its ranks filled with [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|clone pilots]] and operating alongside the [[Jedi Starfighter Corps]], it was equipped with a new collection of advanced starfighters, including the [[V-19 Torrent starfighter/Legends|V-19 Torrent]], the [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-B Y-wing]] and the [[Z-95 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunter]]. Late-war additions to the Starfighter Corps' arsenal included the [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-wing starfighter]], the [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter/Legends|ARC-170 snubfighter]] and the [[NTB-630 naval bomber/Legends|NTB-630]] and [[PTB-625 planetary bomber/Legends|PTB-625]] [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

The Republic Navy's main starfighter carriers of the war, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-]] and [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], were originally designed with traditional doctrine in mind and to operate [[NTB-630 naval bomber/Legends|NTB-630 torpedo bombers]] alongside short-range [[A-6 Interceptor]]s. However, developments in snubfighter technology had outraced doctrine: the performance of [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighters]] at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] had shown that hyperspace-capable snubfighters could indeed destroy battleships. The experience was confirmed with the destruction of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] at the [[Battle of the Kaliida Nebula/Legends|Battle of the Kaliida Nebula]], helped in no small part by it being crippled by Y-wing starfighters. Consequently, carrier capacity was largely given over to snubfighters like the ARC-170 by the end of the Clone Wars, and designers like [[Vors Voorhorian]] and [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]] spent the war years designing a new generation of starfighters that could dogfight on equal terms with any starfighter in space.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

As the Clone Wars progressed, heavy losses among clone pilots and the growing significance of space combat meant that [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] otherwise trained for ground warfare found themselves pressed into pilot roles. Among these units was the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]], which deployed a detachment of pilots to the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] who, alongside [[Squad Seven (Galactic Republic)|Squad Seven]], proved instrumental in breaking through [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] pickets to allow [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] to board the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']] to rescue the kidnapped [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>

===Legacy===
The Starfighter Corps was entirely merged and integrated into the new [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] after the [[Declaration of a New Order]]. Unlike the Republic Navy, the Imperial Navy's doctrine focused on [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] firepower rather than starfighter superiority and it subordinated the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Imperial Starfighter Corps]] to this role. Consequently the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] was often starved of starfighter support, and had to organize fighters loaned from the Navy into understrength [[ground support wing]]s. The Empire turned away from snubfighter development and instead focused on the creation of a new generation of space superiority fighters, culminating in [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]]' [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]] of starfighter. The [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Alliance Starfighter Corps]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], meanwhile, continued development of snubfighters, and was notable in that it remained an entirely independent branch of the [[Alliance Military/Legends|Alliance Military]].<ref name="The Essential Guide to Warfare" />

==Organization==
===Mandalorian Wars and Jedi Civil War===
[[Squadron/Legends|Squadrons]] were the highest organizational unit of the Corps during this period, with each squadron commanded by a [[Commander/Legends|Commander]]. Because of the lack of any larger units, there was a higher turnover rate of this position than in other fields, with many commanders choosing to take assignments on larger ships in order to receive promotions.<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

===Clone Wars===
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] the Corps was divided into Groups, with each group assigned to specific units such as capital ships or starfighter bases:

*'''Group''': A Group was composed of two wings, 72 to 640 starfighters plus support crews, and commanded by a clone commander and a [[Senior Jedi General]].
*'''Wing''': A Wing was of 3 to 10 squadrons, 36 to 320 starfighters plus support crews, and command by a clone commander or [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]].
*'''Squadron''': A Squadron was composed of 3 to 4 flights, 12 to 32 starfighters plus support crews, and commanded by a [[Major/Legends|Major]] or [[Jedi Commander/Legends|Jedi Commander]].
*'''Flight''': A Flight was composed of 2 sections, 4 to 8 starfighters plus support crews, and command by a [[Captain/Legends|Captain]].
*'''Section''': A Section was commanded by a [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] and composed of 2 to 4 starfighters.
